findings.F1: Across all six coins, a day's volume against its prior 30-day mean volume ranks positively with the coin's excess return over the next 5 days. On the non-overlapping 5-day grid the Spearman correlation is 0.0595 (p=0.0015, n=2843 independent cases). This holds on both sides of the day's move: on up days the volume ratio's Spearman is 0.061 (p=0.024, n=1365), and on down days it is 0.0565 (p=0.030, n=1476). On down days the OLS coefficient on the log volume ratio is 0.0110 (t=2.04).
findings.F2: The strongest up days on the heaviest volume are followed by the largest excess return. The top quintile of one-day return within the top volume tercile averages +2.13% excess over 5 days (t=2.61, n=293). The same quintile on the thinnest volume averages +0.47% (t=0.47, n=99). This is one cell out of about fifty that were examined, so on its own it is only marginal.
findings.F3: Up days in the top half of standardised size and the top quartile of volume ratio do not hold up as a stable group. They show positive excess in five of six coins (+0.3% to +3.5%; LTC is −0.95%) but no single coin reaches t>1.2. They are positive in both halves of the windows (+0.83% with t=0.88, then +1.66% with t=1.39). The z×volume interaction in OLS has t=1.00.
findings.F4: The tested situation goes the other way. Moderate falls (second return quintile) on the thinnest volume tercile are followed by −1.37% excess over 5 days (t=−2.00, n=221) rather than a rebound. The idea's active cases are strongly negative in 2018 (t=−2.74) and 2019 (t=−5.02), positive in 2020 (t=3.10), and flat afterwards, so their result depends on the year.
findings.F5: Some other angles look notable but cannot be told apart from chance given how many cells were examined.

ideas.idea: When a coin trades more volume today than its own 30-day average daily volume, its price rises more than usual over the next 5 days, more so the larger that volume ratio. This holds whether the day closed up or down.
ideas.consequence: A volume surge against the coin's own recent average is a reason to lean long for the following 5 days, and a thin-volume day is a reason to refuse a long.
ideas.name: Volume surge precedes gains

ideas.idea: When a coin rises sharply over one day on volume above its own 30-day average daily volume, it keeps rising over the next 5 days. The larger the rise and the heavier its volume against that average, the larger the continuation.
ideas.consequence: A sharp rise on heavy volume is a reason to join the move for the next 5 days rather than fade it.
ideas.name: Heavy-volume rallies continue
